what_this_is: B2 hand-verification. For each sampled record I was shown ONLY goal (title+body) and context (alphabetical file union, counts, modules) and judged whether a reader could reconstruct the reference_decomposition -- its number of subtasks and their grouping. Recorded per-record so the rate is auditable rather than asserted.
standard_applied: RECONSTRUCTIBLE = a reader following project convention could produce the same number of subtasks AND substantially the same grouping. Getting the topic right is not reconstruction; getting the SPLIT right is.

judgements.why: 5 subtasks include a changelog rename and a doc explanation added only after review; nothing in goal+context implies either.
12 subtasks over 9 files, of which 'nits', 'nit', 'fix', 'empty commit' are pure review residue.
'iter', 'cln', 'no list as default' are reactions to review, unpredictable from the goal.
8 subtasks on 1 file, two of them merge-from-main commits -- workflow noise, not decomposition.
8 subtasks on 1 doc file. Body has 4 numbered items but they do not map to the commits.
31 subtasks over 2 files. No reader predicts 31 from a doc-cleanup goal.
two of five are merge commits from upstream.
first subtask adds an unrelated core-dev entry; an accidental-file removal follows. Neither is derivable.
24 subtasks of incremental optimisation ('sort first', 'style', 'fix').
WIP PR; subtasks are exploratory ('wip', 'Build one example').
includes a named reviewer's-review commit and a merge; 25 files but only 4 commits -- the ratio itself is unpredictable.

RISK CASE. 3 subtasks are exactly the scikit-learn convention fix -> changelog -> test. A reader who knows the convention and sees n_sub is small could produce this split.

PARTIAL/FLAGGED. A release PR whose body is a 16-checkbox release checklist. The checkboxes are process steps, not the 44 commits, so full reconstruction fails -- but the body is the one place in this sample where the goal text enumerates steps at all, and it is counted against us conservatively.
'fix', 'more typos' -- successive unplanned corrections.

mechanism_found.claim: Reconstruction risk is a function of DECOMPOSITION LENGTH, not of context content.
mechanism_found.evidence: All 3 flagged records are either the minimum length (n_sub=3, two cases) or the one record whose body is literally a checklist. Every record with n_sub>=4 was judged NOT reconstructible.
mechanism_found.why: Long decompositions are dominated by review-cycle residue that did not exist when the goal was written. Measured mechanically over all 121 records: 445/1101 = 0.404 of subtasks match review-noise patterns (nit/fix/wip/cln/style/typo/empty commit or a merge-from-main). A reader cannot predict a reviewer's future comments.
mechanism_found.recommended_use: Routes measuring decomposition strategy against this corpus should either exclude n_sub==3 records or report results split by that boundary. The flag is carried on each record so the choice is explicit.
